app.calc_error: Calculation error. Please try again or reload the page.
app.caption: Navigator's assistant: calculations with step-by-step solutions and maritime theory.
app.load_error: Couldn't load the calculation module — check your internet connection and reload the page.
calc.anchor.caption: The practical depth : chain-length ratio (scope ratio) — does not replace the company's SMS or the master's decision
calc.anchor.hawse_height_label: Hawse pipe height above water, m
calc.anchor.shackle_length_label: Length of one shackle, m (check against the ship's particulars)
calc.anchor.title: Anchor chain length
calc.anchor.warning: The table ratio is a good-seamanship guideline, not a regulation. The final decision on how much chain to pay out rests with the master, taking into account the company's SMS, the bottom, and the weather forecast.
calc.blind_distance.caption: The distance ahead of the stem hidden from the bridge observer by an obstruction (forecastle/deck cargo) — by similar triangles.
calc.blind_distance.distance_label: Distance from observer to obstruction, m
calc.blind_distance.eye_height_label: Height of eye above waterline, m
calc.blind_distance.obstruction_height_l: Height of obstruction above waterline, m
calc.blind_distance.title: Blind Distance Ahead
calc.bunker.caption: Interpolates volume from the tank's calibration table and calculates fuel weight from sounding and density.
calc.bunker.density_label: Fuel density at measured temperature, mt/m³
calc.bunker.disclaimer: No temperature correction (VCF/ASTM Table 54B) — enter density at the measured temperature, not the certificate density at 15°C.
calc.bunker.title: Fuel Quantity by Tank Sounding
calc.common.disclaimer: Advisory calculation. Results do not replace official calculations, the ship's own tables or the navigator's decision.
calc.compass.caption: ΔK = δ + d — total compass correction from deviation and variation
calc.compass.title: Magnetic compass correction
calc.compass.variation_caption: The variation printed on a chart is given for a specific year and changes annually — bring it to the current year of the voyage, the result is substituted into the field below
calc.compass.variation_expander: Bring the chart's variation to the year of the voyage
calc.compass.variation_result: Variation for {year}: {value}°. Substituted into the “Variation d” field below.
calc.compass_comparison.caption: Difference between two simultaneous compass readings (e.g. steering compass and gyrocompass) — a routine check for fault/increasing error.
calc.compass_comparison.disclaimer: The acceptable difference isn't standardised — it's set by the instrument's manual and the ship's SMS. If the difference is unusually large or growing watch to watch, report it to the master/chief mate.
calc.compass_comparison.title: Compass Comparison
calc.coords_converter.caption: Decimal degrees ↔ degrees, minutes, seconds
calc.coords_converter.title: Coordinate Converter
calc.cpa.caption: Vector plot of relative motion — as on a maneuvering board/ARPA.
calc.cpa.tcpa_negative_warning: TCPA is negative — the target is already receding; the closest point of approach was in the past.
calc.cpa.title: CPA/TCPA — closing with a target
calc.dew_point.caption: Dew point via the Magnus-Tetens formula, plus two independent practical rules for deciding whether to ventilate a cargo hold.
calc.dew_point.dew_point_header: 1. Dew point from temperature and humidity
calc.dew_point.dew_point_rule_caption: Ventilate ONLY if the outside air's dew point is LOWER than the hold air's dew point.
calc.dew_point.hold_dew_point_label: Dew point of the air in the hold, °C
calc.dew_point.outside_dew_point_label: Dew point of the outside air, °C
calc.dew_point.result_borderline: The dew point difference is 0 — a borderline case; the decision is the OOW's/master's.
calc.dew_point.three_degree_caption: Ventilate ONLY if the outside air is at least 3°C colder than the cargo.
calc.dew_point.title: Dew Point / Hold Ventilation
calc.draft.ballast_label: Ballast, t (enter the final figure yourself — see the tank helper below)
calc.draft.caption: The full method: 2 surveys (INITIAL before cargo operations, FINAL after), 1st- and 2nd-order trim corrections, cargo = the difference between the surveys' net displacements. Reproduced from a real working methodology.
calc.draft.constant_caption: Net displacement (INITIAL) − Lightship — the unaccounted remainder
calc.draft.deductibles_caption: A free-form list — rename/add/remove rows for your own ship (heavy fuel oil, diesel oil, lube oil, fresh water, sewage, etc.).
calc.draft.disp_high_label: Displacement at the higher draft, t
calc.draft.disp_low_label: Displacement at the lower draft, t
calc.draft.dist_aft_label: Aft mark to aft perpendicular, m (“+” if the mark is forward of AP)
calc.draft.dist_fwd_label: Forward mark to forward perpendicular, m (“−” if the mark is aft of FP)
calc.draft.dist_mid_label: Midship mark to amidships, m (“+” if the mark is forward)
calc.draft.drafts_header: Drafts, m (port/starboard at forward, midships, aft)
calc.draft.hydrostatic_caption: First estimate the draft, find the lower/upper bound in the ship's table, then enter the displacement for each
calc.draft.hydrostatic_header: Hydrostatic table — the two nearest values to the true draft
calc.draft.initial_missing_warning: Calculate the initial draft first (Step 1) — there is nothing to compare the cargo against otherwise.
calc.draft.lcf_tpc_mct_header: LCF, TPC, MCT (from the hydrostatic table, at a draft close to the true one)
calc.draft.method_label: Perpendicular-reduction scheme (depends on where the draft marks are located on the ship)
calc.draft.methodology_info: The method (6 sounding points, reduction to perpendiculars, trim and density corrections) is the same for any ship. Enter your ship's data: LBP, draft mark positions, hydrostatics, TPC/MCT. Default values are an example of a real survey.
calc.draft.profile_caption: The profile stores only the parameters that don't change for the ship (LBP, draft-mark positions, reduction scheme). Drafts, TPC/MCT, deductibles are entered fresh for each survey — they are not part of the profile. The “Download vessel profile” button is at the bottom of the tab.
calc.draft.profile_expander: Vessel profile (LBP, mark positions, scheme) — save/load
calc.draft.profile_loaded: Profile loaded — the ship parameter values below have been updated.
calc.draft.report_caption: Built from the calculated INITIAL/FINAL surveys. The Word file (.docx) is for editing, sending and archiving; the printout can be saved as PDF.
calc.draft.tanks_caption: Volume is what's already been read off the tank's calibration table from the actual sounding (each ship/tank has its own table, not reproduced here). This is only a helper: the sum calculated here must be checked and entered into the “Ballast” field above yourself — there is no automatic substitution, deliberately, to avoid ending up with a physically impossible number (this was observed in a real file — the tank figures and the report total disagreed).
calc.draft.tanks_expander: Calculate ballast from tanks (for reference — NOT substituted automatically)
calc.draft.tanks_sum_caption: Sum across tanks: {total} t (entered in the “Ballast” field: {ballast} t)
calc.draft.title: Draft Survey
calc.drift.caption: Vector solution: either the course/speed made good with a known heading, or the course to steer to make a given track.
calc.drift.mode_course_to_steer: Course to steer — to make a given track
calc.drift.mode_resultant: Course and speed over ground (COG/SOG) — from a known heading
calc.drift.title: Set and drift — dead reckoning triangle
calc.log.caption: Distance run from log readings, determining the log coefficient on a measured mile, and dead reckoning position from course and distance.
calc.log.coefficient_caption: From a known actual distance (e.g. on a measured mile / by fixed landmarks) and the log difference over the same interval: Kl = actual distance / log difference.
calc.log.distance_caption: S = log difference × Kl, where log difference = Log2 - Log1.
calc.log.dr_distance_hint: Defaults to the last S calculated above — you can enter your own value.
calc.log.position_caption: Point of departure + constant course + distance run → arrival point (Mercator/rhumb-line dead reckoning).
calc.log.title: Dead Reckoning by Log
calc.multi_eta.caption: Sequential legs (distance + speed) from departure to the final point — total time and ETA at each waypoint.
calc.multi_eta.title: Multi-Waypoint ETA
calc.noon_report.caption: Daily passage figures: average speed, daily fuel consumption, remaining fuel on board, and time to go.
calc.noon_report.title: Noon Report
calc.opposite_draft.caption: Reduces draft marks read on deck to the perpendiculars (forward/midships/aft) — the same method used in draft survey.
calc.opposite_draft.dist_aft_label: Aft mark to aft perpendicular, m (“+” if forward of AP)
calc.opposite_draft.dist_fwd_label: Forward mark to forward perpendicular, m (“−” if aft of FP)
calc.opposite_draft.dist_mid_label: Midship mark to amidships, m (“+” if forward)
calc.opposite_draft.title: Perpendicular Draft Reduction
calc.roll_gm.caption: Estimate of GM from the free rolling period in calm water. With length and draft — IMO formula; without them — simplified.
calc.roll_gm.disclaimer: Rolling-period estimate (IMO IS Code 2008, Part A, 2.3.4); accuracy ±15–20 %. Not a substitute for the ship's stability calculation.
calc.roll_gm.title: GM Estimate from Roll Period
calc.sailing.caption: Distance and course between two points along the great-circle arc (shortest path) and along a line of constant course
calc.sailing.steps_great_circle: Show the calculation steps — great circle
calc.sailing.steps_rhumb_line: Show the calculation steps — rhumb line
calc.sailing.title: Great Circle / Rhumb Line
calc.sextant.caption: Dip of the visible horizon and reduction of the sextant reading to apparent altitude (Ha = Hs + IC − Dip). The main correction (refraction/parallax/semi-diameter) uses Nautical Almanac tables and is not computed here.
calc.sextant.disclaimer: Main correction (refraction/parallax/semi-diameter from the Nautical Almanac) not included — only Dip and IC.
calc.sextant.ic_hint: Sign of IC: index error on the arc → enter IC as negative; off the arc → positive.
calc.sextant.title: Sextant Altitude Corrections
calc.squat.caption: Simplified Barrass rule of thumb: open water / confined channel. Speed is through the water. The Under Keel Clearance tab already includes squat — do not subtract it twice.
calc.squat.title: Squat — shallow-water sinkage
calc.squat.warning: This is an ESTIMATE, not a precise hydrodynamic calculation. For critical transits (small UKC, narrow/shallow channel), a more accurate method or pilotage data is required.
calc.stability.caption: Initial metacentric height (GM) and the list/new KG when cargo is loaded, discharged, or shifted. Small-angle formulas (valid up to roughly 10° of list) — see the warning below.
calc.stability.cargo_kg_label: Height of the cargo's CG above the keel (kg of cargo), m
calc.stability.cargo_op_caption: If cargo is loaded/discharged or shifted vertically, the new KG is recalculated here. If it is also shifted transversely, the new list is calculated below using this new KG.
calc.stability.gm_for_list_label: GM for the list calculation, m
calc.stability.gm_negative_error: GM is negative — negative initial stability. Report to the master immediately.
calc.stability.kg_label: KG (current, from the cargo plan), m
calc.stability.km_label: KM (from the ship's tables at the current draft), m
calc.stability.list_caption: Uses the GM calculated above at the current/new KG (if there was a cargo operation, recalculate GM with the new KG before this step).
calc.stability.list_header: List from a transverse cargo shift
calc.stability.op_vertical_shift: Vertical shift of cargo (ship's mass unchanged)
calc.stability.title: Stability — GM and list from shifting cargo
calc.stability.transverse_distance_label: Transverse shift of the weight moment from the centreline, m
calc.stability.warning: This is NOT a substitute for the mandatory check against the ship's own “Stability Information for the Master”, and it does not verify compliance with the IMO IS Code 2008 criteria — there is no hull-form data here to confirm that. A GM below zero is a critical situation (negative stability); the decision remains with the master/chief mate.
calc.std.caption: S = V × t — the basic dead-reckoning problem
calc.std.title: Speed / Time / Distance / ETA
calc.tides.caption: The rule of twelfths — an approximate interpolation from the port's tide tables
calc.tides.half_cycle_end_header: End of the half-cycle (the next high or low water)
calc.tides.half_cycle_start_header: Start of the half-cycle (low or high water from the tide table)
calc.tides.target_header: The moment you need the height for
calc.tides.title: Tide height between low and high water
calc.trim_density.caption: First-order trim correction (LCF/TPC) and water density correction — the same method used in draft survey, as a standalone tool.
calc.trim_density.displacement_table_lab: Tabulated displacement for the corrected mean draft, t
calc.trim_density.title: Displacement Trim/Density Correction
calc.true_wind.caption: Converts apparent (underway) wind into true wind using the ship's speed vector.
calc.true_wind.title: True Wind
calc.ukc.caption: Accounts for heel, squat under way, and an allowance for sea state
calc.ukc.result_ok: Clearance is sufficient. UKC = {ukc} m (margin {margin} m)
calc.ukc.title: Under Keel Clearance (UKC)
calc.unit_converter.caption: Speed, distance, depth, volume — no formulas to remember
calc.unit_converter.title: Unit Converter
err.converters.coords.bad_hemisphere: Hemisphere must be N, S, E, or W
err.converters.coords.negative_component: Degrees, minutes, and seconds cannot be negative — sign is set by the hemisphere choice
err.draft.draft_high_equals_low: draft_high and draft_low must not be equal
err.dew_point.humidity_out_of_range: Relative humidity must be greater than 0 and no more than 100%
err.drift.no_course_solution: At this speed through the water and this drift, the ship cannot make the given track (the drift is stronger than the ship's speed in this direction).
err.drift.no_valid_solution: No physically meaningful solution found (a positive speed over ground).
err.log.rol_zero: The log difference cannot be zero when determining the log coefficient
err.stability.discharge_exceeds_displace: The weight of cargo to discharge cannot exceed the displacement
err.stability.gm_must_be_positive: GM must be positive — the small-angle formula does not apply when GM ≤ 0 (see the warning)
err.std.deadline_not_in_future: The deadline must be later than the current time — check the date/time entered
err.std.no_waypoints: Add at least one route leg with a distance and speed
err.std.speed_zero: Speed cannot be zero when calculating time
err.std.time_zero: Time cannot be zero when calculating speed
err.tides.end_before_start: The half-cycle end time must be later than the start time
report.draft.corrected_drafts_label: Corrected draft fwd / mid / aft, m
report.draft.dist_aft_label: Aft mark to aft perpendicular, m
report.draft.dist_fwd_label: Forward mark to forward perpendicular, m
report.draft.title: Draft Survey — {vessel}
theory.caption: Official texts, practitioner's commentary, diagrams and interactive scenes
theory.content_disclaimer: An educational summary in plain language, not the official text of the document. Before an exam or real-world use, check it against the current edition of the source.
theory.missing_translation_note: This topic is not yet translated into the selected language — showing the Russian text.
theory.planned_warning: “{title}” is still being written — content will appear here later.
theory.verify_caption: The exact figures in this point should be double-checked against the official text
tooltip.anchor-condition: Anchoring conditions (weather, holding ground, duration) — sets the recommended depth-to-chain ratio.
tooltip.anchor-depth: Depth at the anchoring spot from the chart/echo sounder, metres.
tooltip.anchor-hawse: Height of the hawse pipe above the water at current draft, metres.
tooltip.anchor-ratio: Ratio of (depth+hawse) to chain length — pre-filled from the chosen condition, editable.
tooltip.anchor-shackle-length: Length of one shackle of chain per the ship's particulars (usually 25–27.5 m, but check your own ship's data).
tooltip.bd-distance: Distance from the conning position to the obstruction along the deck, metres.
tooltip.bd-eye-height: Height of the conning position observer's eye above the waterline, metres.
tooltip.bd-obstruction-height: Height of the obstruction (forecastle, cargo, superstructure) blocking the view, above the waterline, metres.
tooltip.bunker-density: Fuel density AT THE MEASURED TEMPERATURE (not the certificate density at 15°C) — measure it with a hydrometer at the same time as the sounding.
tooltip.bunker-sounding: The tank sounding (fuel level) as measured by tape or gauge, cm.
tooltip.cc-decimal: Coordinate in decimal degrees (e.g. 59.5) — N/E positive, S/W negative.
tooltip.cc-hemisphere: The coordinate's hemisphere (N/S for latitude, E/W for longitude).
tooltip.cc-is-latitude: Latitude or longitude — determines the valid hemispheres (N/S or E/W).
tooltip.cpa-target-bearing: Bearing to the target at the moment of observation — from radar/ARPA or visually.
tooltip.cpa-target-course: Target's course — from radar/ARPA (relative motion vector) or estimated.
tooltip.cpa-target-range: Range to the target at the moment of observation, nautical miles.
tooltip.drift-course: The heading the ship is actually steering through the water.
tooltip.drift-set: Set — the direction the current/drift is going toward, ° true.
tooltip.drift-speed-water-1: Ship's speed through the water (by log), knots.
tooltip.drift-speed-water-2: Ship's speed through the water (by log), knots.
tooltip.drift-track: The desired track (course over ground) you need to make good.
tooltip.ds-dist-aft: Distance from the aft draft mark to the aft perpendicular. Positive if the mark is forward of AP (the usual case).
tooltip.ds-dist-fwd: Distance from the forward draft mark to the forward perpendicular (from the ship's draft-mark plan). Negative if the mark is aft of FP (the usual case).
tooltip.ds-dist-mid: Distance from the midship mark to amidships. Positive if the mark is forward of amidships; 0 if exactly amidships.
tooltip.ds-lbp: Length between perpendiculars (LBP), metres — from the ship's particulars.
tooltip.ds-lightship: Lightship weight, tonnes — from the ship's tonnage certificate/stability booklet.
tooltip.ds-method: The layout scheme of the draft marks relative to the perpendiculars on this ship — see the ship's drawings/draft mark plan.
tooltip.ds-table-step: The draft step (increment) of the ship's hydrostatic table, metres — usually 0.01 or 0.1.
tooltip.ds-vessel-name: Ship's name — for the report header only, doesn't affect the calculation.
tooltip.cmp-heading-a: The first compass's reading (e.g. steering/master compass) at the moment of comparison, °.
tooltip.cmp-heading-b: The second compass's reading (e.g. gyrocompass) at the same moment, °.
tooltip.dpr-hold: Dew point of the air in the hold's headspace — worked out from the T and RH measured inside the hold.
tooltip.dp-humidity: Relative humidity of the air, % — from a hygrometer/psychrometer.
tooltip.tdr-cargo-temp: Mean cargo temperature recorded at loading (usually from the cargo documents/a probe thermometer).
tooltip.dpr-outside: Dew point of the outside air — either read from the ship's barometer/hygrometer, or calculated above from T and RH.
tooltip.tdr-outside-temp: Outside air temperature (dry bulb) at the time of the check, °C.
tooltip.input-deviation: Compass deviation on this heading — taken from the ship's deviation table.
tooltip.input-heading: Ship's heading (compass, gyro, or true — depending on which direction you're converting).
tooltip.input-variation: Magnetic variation in this area — from the chart, or from the "correct to voyage year" tool above.
tooltip.log-actual-distance: Actual distance covered on a measured mile or between known landmarks — known in advance, not from the log.
tooltip.log-dr-course: Course made good (heading corrected for leeway/current) the ship is steering.
tooltip.log-dr-distance: Distance run by dead reckoning (usually from the log, corrected).
tooltip.log-dr-lat1: Latitude of the departure point (last known position).
tooltip.log-ol1: Log reading at the start of the run (read from the instrument).
tooltip.log-ol2: Log reading at the end of the run.
tooltip.log-rol-input: Difference of log readings (OL2 − OL1) — enter directly if already calculated.
tooltip.meta-departure-date: Departure date / start of the route.
tooltip.noon-distance-run: Distance covered during the reporting period (usually 24h) — by log/GPS.
tooltip.noon-distance-to-go: Distance remaining to the destination — needed only for endurance/time-to-go (optional).
tooltip.noon-elapsed-hours: Length of the reporting period, hours (usually 24, but a partial day works too).
tooltip.noon-fuel-consumed: Fuel consumed during the reporting period, metric tonnes — from the engine log.
tooltip.noon-rob-before: Fuel remaining on board at the start of the period (ROB), tonnes.
tooltip.od-dist-aft: Distance from the aft mark to the aft perpendicular. Positive if the mark is forward of AP.
tooltip.od-dist-fwd: Distance from the forward mark to the forward perpendicular. Negative if the mark is aft of FP.
tooltip.od-dist-mid: Distance from the midship mark to amidships. Positive if forward; 0 if exactly amidships.
tooltip.od-mean-aft: Draft read at the aft mark, metres.
tooltip.od-mean-fwd: Draft read at the forward mark, metres.
tooltip.od-mean-mid: Draft read at the midships mark, metres.
tooltip.od-method: The layout of this ship's draft marks relative to the perpendiculars.
tooltip.rg-period: Full rolling period (port–stbd–port), seconds: time several full cycles in calm water and divide by their number. Do not use a half period — GM would come out 4 times too large.
tooltip.sailing-lat1: Latitude of the departure point, decimal degrees (N positive, S negative).
tooltip.sailing-lat2: Latitude of the destination point, decimal degrees.
tooltip.sailing-lon1: Longitude of the departure point, decimal degrees (E positive, W negative).
tooltip.sailing-lon2: Longitude of the destination point, decimal degrees.
tooltip.squat-cb: Ship's block coefficient Cb — from the ship's particulars.
tooltip.st-displacement: Ship's current displacement, tonnes — from the hydrostatic table for the current draft.
tooltip.st-kg: Height of the centre of gravity above keel (KG) — from the current loading plan/stability calculation.
tooltip.st-km: Height of the metacentre above keel (KM) at the current draft — from the hydrostatic table.
tooltip.st-ld-weight: Weight of cargo being loaded or discharged, tonnes.
tooltip.st-ld-weight-kg: Height of the cargo's own centre of gravity above keel, metres.
tooltip.st-list-distance: Transverse distance the weight's moment is shifted from the centreline, metres.
tooltip.st-list-gm: Ship's current metacentric height GM, metres.
tooltip.st-list-weight: Weight of cargo whose moment is being shifted across the ship, tonnes.
tooltip.st-vs-distance: Vertical shift distance of the cargo, metres ("+" up, "−" down).
tooltip.st-vs-weight: Weight of cargo being shifted vertically (total ship weight unchanged), tonnes.
tooltip.std-distance-time: Time under way, hours (decimals allowed, e.g. 2.5 h = 2h 30min).
tooltip.std-eta-date: Current date (the date the calculation is made from).
tooltip.std-eta-distance: Distance remaining to the arrival point, nautical miles.
tooltip.std-eta-speed: Expected speed for the passage, knots.
tooltip.std-reqspeed-deadline-date: The date you must arrive by (e.g. lock opening, pilot station slot).
tooltip.std-reqspeed-deadline-time: The time you must arrive by.
tooltip.std-reqspeed-distance: Remaining distance to the arrival point, nautical miles.
tooltip.std-speed-distance: Distance covered or required, nautical miles.
tooltip.sx-height: Height of eye above sea level, metres — how high the observer's deck/bridge position is.
tooltip.sx-hs: The raw sextant reading off the limb — exactly what you read off the instrument, before any corrections.
tooltip.sx-ic: The sextant's index correction — found by checking against the horizon or a star before observing (see the sextant's calibration log).
tooltip.td-density: Actual density of the water at the survey location, mt/m³ — measured with a hydrometer.
tooltip.td-displacement: Displacement from the hydrostatic table for the draft amidships (before corrections), tonnes.
tooltip.td-lcf: Distance of the centre of flotation (LCF) from amidships at the current draft, metres — from the hydrostatic table.
tooltip.td-tpc: Tonnes per centimetre immersion (TPC) at this draft — from the hydrostatic table.
tooltip.td-trim: Ship's trim (draft aft minus draft forward), metres.
tooltip.theory-topic-select: Choose a theory topic to study.
tooltip.tides-end-height: Sea level height at the end of the tidal phase (the next low or high water), metres.
tooltip.tides-end-time: Time of the next high/low water — from tide tables.
tooltip.tides-start-height: Sea level height at the start of the tidal phase (high or low water), metres — from tide tables.
tooltip.tides-start-time: Time of the high/low water the calculation starts from — from tide tables.
tooltip.tides-target-time: The moment in time you need the tide height for.
tooltip.tw-awa: The angle the apparent wind is coming from — from the anemometer/visually, 0° = dead ahead.
tooltip.tw-aws: Wind speed shown by the anemometer while under way (apparent, not true wind).
tooltip.tw-heading: Ship's true heading — needed only for the true wind DIRECTION (optional if the angle alone is enough).
tooltip.tw-speed: Ship's speed by log or GPS, knots.
tooltip.uc-from-unit: The unit the value is currently in.
tooltip.uc-value: The number to convert into another unit.
tooltip.ukc-beam: Ship's beam at midships, metres — needed to work out the draft increase from heel.
tooltip.ukc-block-coefficient: Block coefficient Cb — from the ship's particulars (typically 0.65–0.85 for cargo ships/tankers).
tooltip.ukc-channel-area: Cross-sectional area of the channel at this point, m² — from the chart/fairway sailing directions.
tooltip.ukc-charted-depth: Charted depth at the transit point, metres.
tooltip.ukc-required-minimum: Minimum under-keel clearance required by company policy or port regulations, metres.
tooltip.ukc-ship-underwater-area: Underwater cross-sectional area of the ship at midships, m² (roughly draft × beam × midship coefficient).
tooltip.ukc-speed: Ship's speed through the transit, knots — needed for the squat calculation.
tooltip.ukc-static-draft: Ship's static draft right now (no heel/squat), metres.
tooltip.ukc-tide-height: Tide height at the time of transit (from tide tables or the Tides calculator), metres.
tooltip.ukc-wave-allowance: Extra depth allowance for wave action — per company/port policy or your own judgement, metres.
tooltip.variation-annual-change: Annual change of variation — also printed on the chart next to the variation value (e.g. "increasing 0.1° per year").
tooltip.variation-chart-value: The variation printed on the chart itself, as of the chart's date.
tooltip.variation-chart-year: The year the chart's printed variation refers to (usually shown next to the variation value in the chart's corner).
tooltip.variation-target-year: The year you want the variation corrected to (usually the current voyage year).

calc.ullage.title: Cargo by Tank Ullage (Liquid Cargo)
calc.ullage.caption: Tank level → volume from calibration table → correction to 15°C (VCF) → cargo mass.
calc.ullage.disclaimer: VCF follows the ASTM D1250-80 Table 54B procedure (refined products, 653–1075 kg/m³) without the standard's step rounding; mass is in vacuo, weight in air (WCF) is shown below. Use certified tables / tanker software for commercial cargo.
err.cargo_ullage.table_too_short: The calibration table must have at least 2 rows.
err.cargo_ullage.density_out_of_range: Density at 15 °C is outside ASTM Table 54B (653–1075 kg/m³).
err.cargo_ullage.density_must_be_positiv: Density must be a positive number.
err.cargo_ullage.tank_depth_required: Tank depth is required for an ullage measurement.
err.cargo_ullage.ullage_exceeds_tank_dep: Ullage cannot exceed the tank depth.

app.about.title: About
app.about.description: Navigation and cargo calculations, maritime theory and a COLREGs trainer for deck officers. Works offline. Results are supplementary and do not replace official calculations or the officer's own judgment.
app.about.changelog.1: COLREGs trainer — 40 situations: added vessels at anchor and aground, pilot, towing, trawling and other fishing vessels, vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre and constrained by draught — by day and by night from lights; sailing vessels at night; manoeuvring and fog sound signals.
app.about.changelog.2: iPhone and iPad version: installed from Safari to the Home Screen, works offline. One key covers a computer and one phone: Android or iPhone/iPad.
app.about.changelog.3: Everything you enter is saved automatically: the drill log, values and results of every calculator, the selected theory topic — after closing, the app reopens where you left off. Windows version: full screen without a frame (F11).
app.about.changelog.4: New AZIMUTH look: launch animation, black-and-gold icon and logo.
app.about.changelog.5: Compass error by the Sun: true bearing by azimuth (any time) and by amplitude (sunrise/sunset), no almanac or tables, with deviation.
app.about.disclaimer: A training/support tool. Calculation results and theory content do not replace official sources, ship's tables, or the officer's own judgment.
calc.ballast_sounding.title: Remaining Ballast with Heel and Trim Corrections
calc.ballast_sounding.caption: Volume from the calibration table (entered already looked up) + trim/heel corrections from the ship's own tables → ballast mass by tank.
calc.ballast_sounding.conditions_header: Overall ship condition at the time of sounding
calc.ballast_sounding.conditions_hint: One trim and one heel value for the whole calculation (this is a ship condition, not a per-tank value). Sign convention follows your own ship's correction tables.
calc.ballast_sounding.disclaimer: Volume and trim/heel correction rates are figures from your own ship's calibration/ballast tables (specific to each tank/ship), entered manually. The calculator only applies the formula V_corr = V_obs + trim_rate×trim + heel_rate×heel — it does not replace the ship's own tables or the officer's judgment.
err.ballast_sounding.density_must_be_pos: Density must be a positive number.
err.ballast_sounding.corrected_volume_ne: The corrected volume came out negative — check the sign of the corrections and the entered volume.
err.ballast_sounding.no_tanks: There is no tank with a name and a non-zero volume.
calc.drill_log.title: Ship Drill Log
calc.drill_log.caption: Drill name + periodicity + date last performed → next due date and status. Saved automatically.
calc.drill_log.manual_hint: date not calculated — tied to the actual crew change
calc.drill_log.disclaimer: You choose each drill's periodicity yourself, per your company's SMS. "Monthly", "quarterly", "semi-annual" and "annual" are counted in calendar months. "On crew change" — the next date is not calculated. Data is stored only on this device.
calc.deadweight_scale.title: Tonnage by Draft (Deadweight Scale)
calc.deadweight_scale.caption: Displacement, TPC and MTC at current draft — linear interpolation from the ship's deadweight scale
calc.deadweight_scale.table_header: Ship's deadweight scale (draft → displacement / TPC / MTC)
calc.deadweight_scale.disclaimer: The table is this ship's own deadweight scale / hydrostatic table (entered by you) — the calculator only interpolates linearly between the rows you enter.
calc.fwa.title: FWA / DWA — Fresh Water Allowance
calc.fwa.caption: Fresh Water Allowance and Dock Water Allowance from displacement, TPC and dock water density
calc.fwa.disclaimer: Standard FWA/DWA formula (Barrass & Derrett) — does not replace the ship's load line and actual draft monitoring.
calc.suspended_load.title: Suspended Load on Crane — GM Loss
calc.suspended_load.caption: Temporary loss of stability while a load is suspended from a crane/derrick (Effect of a Suspended Weight)
calc.suspended_load.height_label: Height of the point of suspension above the weight's original position, m
calc.suspended_load.warning: Negative stability! Lifting this load under these conditions is not safe.
calc.suspended_load.disclaimer: Simplified training model — does not replace the ship's stability information and lifting plan.
err.deadweight_scale.table_too_short: The table must have at least 2 rows
err.deadweight_scale.draft_out_of_range: Draft is outside the range of the entered table
err.fwa.tpc_must_be_positive: TPC must be greater than zero
err.fwa.displacement_must_be_positive: Displacement must be greater than zero
err.fwa.density_must_be_positive: Density must be greater than zero
err.suspended_load.displacement_must_be_: Displacement must be greater than zero
tooltip.dws-draft: Current mean draft of the ship — read off the draft marks/draft gauges alongside
tooltip.fwa-displacement: Current displacement — from the deadweight scale or the latest draft calculation
tooltip.fwa-tpc: Tonnes per cm immersion at the current displacement — from the ship's deadweight scale/hydrostatic table
tooltip.fwa-density: Dock/port water density — measured with a hydrometer alongside
tooltip.sl-displacement: Ship's displacement at the time of lifting, including the load being lifted
tooltip.sl-gm: Ship's GM before the lift begins — from the stability information
tooltip.sl-weight: Weight of the load being lifted by the crane/derrick
tooltip.sl-height: Vertical distance from the weight's original centre of gravity (on deck / in the hold) to the derrick head or crane hook. If the weight is lifted from the quay, use the distance from the ship's G (KG) to the point of suspension.
scene.head_on.s1: Two power-driven vessels meet on reciprocal courses. At night each sees the other's masthead lights in line and both sidelights — a Rule 14 situation.
scene.head_on.s2: Each vessel alters course to STARBOARD and signals the manoeuvre with one short blast (Rule 34(a)).
scene.head_on.s3: They pass port to port at a safe distance. When in doubt whether such a situation exists, assume it does (14(c)).
scene.head_on.s4: Once finally past and clear, both return to their original courses.
scene.crossing.s1: Courses cross and the compass bearing does not change — risk of collision exists (Rule 7(d)(i)).
scene.crossing.s2: The vessel which has the other on her own STARBOARD side keeps out of the way (Rule 15). At night she sees the other's red sidelight.
scene.crossing.s3: Action is early and substantial (Rule 16): a turn to starboard passing astern, not ahead of the other vessel.
scene.crossing.s4: The stand-on vessel keeps her course and speed (Rule 17(a)(i)). The give-way vessel resumes course when the passing is safe.
scene.overtaking.s1: A vessel comes up from more than 22.5° abaft the beam: at night she sees only the sternlight of the other. She is overtaking (Rule 13(b)).
scene.overtaking.s2: The overtaking vessel keeps out of the way of the vessel being overtaken — on whichever side is safe (13(a)).
scene.overtaking.s3: The vessel being overtaken keeps her course and speed (Rule 17).
scene.overtaking.s4: The duty to keep clear remains until she is finally past and clear (13(d)).
scene.narrow_channel.s1: In a narrow channel each vessel keeps as near to the outer limit on her starboard side as is safe and practicable (Rule 9(a)).
scene.narrow_channel.s2: Vessels meeting in the channel pass port to port, each on her own side.
scene.narrow_channel.s3: A sailing vessel or a vessel under 20 m shall not impede a vessel that can navigate safely only within the channel (9(b)).
scene.narrow_channel.s4: Cross the channel only when it does not impede vessels in it (9(d)) — at right angles and quickly.
scene.restricted_visibility.s1: Restricted visibility: safe speed, engines ready for immediate manoeuvre (19(b)), one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes (35(a)).
scene.restricted_visibility.s2: The other vessel is detected by radar alone — determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing and whether risk of collision exists (19(d)).
scene.restricted_visibility.s3: The target is forward of the beam and not being overtaken — avoid altering to PORT (19(d)(i)). Alter to starboard, early and large enough to show on radar.
scene.restricted_visibility.s4: On hearing a fog signal apparently forward of the beam, reduce to the minimum steerage speed and, if necessary, take all way off (19(e)).
scene.light_sectors.s1: Masthead light shows over 225°, each sidelight over 112.5°, the sternlight over 135° (Rule 21). The observer walks round the vessel.
scene.light_sectors.s2: Right ahead: masthead lights in line and both sidelights, red and green.
scene.light_sectors.s3: From starboard the green sidelight is seen, from port the red. The limit is 22.5° abaft the beam.
scene.light_sectors.s4: From more than 22.5° abaft the beam only the sternlight is seen — this is how overtaking is defined (Rule 13).
theory.no_official_annex: The full official text of this annex is not reproduced here — summary below.
theory.no_official_en: Official English text of this rule is not included — summary below.
theory.content_disclaimer_official: The official text is reproduced verbatim (corrected source typos are listed under «Sources»). Commentary and scenes are explanations, not part of the official text.
scene.iala.safe_N: Pass north of the N mark
scene.iala.safe_E: Pass east of the E mark
scene.iala.safe_S: Pass south of the S mark
scene.iala.safe_W: Pass west of the W mark
scene.iala_lateral.s1: The direction of buoyage runs from seaward towards the harbour. Entering, a vessel keeps port-hand marks to port and starboard-hand marks to starboard.
scene.iala_lateral.s2a: Region A (Europe, Africa, most of Asia): port-hand marks are red cans, starboard-hand marks are green cones.
scene.iala_lateral.s2b: Region B (the Americas, Japan, Korea, the Philippines): the colours are reversed — port hand green, starboard hand red. The shapes stay the same.
scene.iala_lateral.s3: At night a mark is recognised by colour and rhythm: red on port-hand marks, green on starboard-hand marks (reversed in Region B). Any rhythm except Fl(2+1).
scene.iala_lateral.s4: Leaving harbour everything is mirrored: Region A red marks are left to starboard. Switch on “Night” and “Region B” to compare.
scene.iala_cardinal.s1: A cardinal mark is placed in a quadrant of the danger. Its name is the side on which it is safe to pass.
scene.iala_cardinal.s2: Topmarks are two black cones: N points up, S points down, E base to base (diamond), W point to point (“wineglass”).
scene.iala_cardinal.s3: The colouring follows the cones: black is where the points are. N — black above, S — black below, E — black outer bands, W — yellow ends.
scene.iala_cardinal.s4: Lights are white, quick flashing: N continuous, E groups of 3 (3 o'clock), S groups of 6 + long flash (6 o'clock), W groups of 9 (9 o'clock).
scene.light_characters.s1: The lights run in real rhythm. On the right — one period: bright segments are light, the cyan marker is the current moment.
scene.light_characters.s2: Flashing — light shorter than darkness; occulting — the opposite; isophase — light and darkness equal.
scene.light_characters.s3: The period is measured from the start of one flash (group) to the start of the next. On the chart: Fl(2) 6s — two flashes every 6 seconds.
scene.gmdss_sea_areas.s1: Sea area A1 — within range of at least one VHF coast station with DSC (typically 20–30 nm). VHF, NAVTEX, EPIRB and SART are enough.
scene.gmdss_sea_areas.s2: Sea area A2 — outside A1 but within range of an MF coast station with DSC (about 100–150 nm). An MF DSC set is added.
scene.gmdss_sea_areas.s3: Sea area A3 — outside A1 and A2, within coverage of the recognized mobile satellite service fitted on board (SOLAS ch. IV from 2024). For Inmarsat roughly 70°N — 70°S. A satellite station or MF/HF is required.
scene.gmdss_sea_areas.s4: Sea area A4 — everything outside A1–A3. In polar waters an Inmarsat ship loses the geostationary satellite — communication is MF/HF DSC (Iridium also covers polar waters).
scene.dsc.mayday: MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY|THIS IS MV AZIMUTH, AZIMUTH, AZIMUTH|MMSI 273 123 456|POSITION 44°35' N 037°22' E|FIRE IN ENGINE ROOM|REQUIRE IMMEDIATE ASSISTANCE. OVER
scene.dsc_distress.s1: Lift the cover and hold the DISTRESS button for 5 seconds. If time allows, select the nature of distress first (fire, flooding…).
scene.dsc_distress.s2: The DSC distress alert goes to all stations on channel 70 with the MMSI and position. Until acknowledged, the set repeats it automatically.
scene.dsc_distress.s3: A coast station acknowledges by DSC. Ships normally do not acknowledge by DSC — they wait for the voice message on channel 16.
scene.dsc_distress.s4: Right after the alert — the distress message by voice on channel 16: MAYDAY ×3, name, MMSI, position, nature of distress, assistance required.
scene.dsc_distress.s5: The Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) organises assistance; nearby ships acknowledge by voice and proceed to the position.
scene.bft.no_waves: No waves — sea like a mirror
bft.sea.1: ripples with the appearance of scales, no foam crests
bft.sea.2: small wavelets, crests of glassy appearance, not breaking
bft.sea.3: large wavelets, crests begin to break, scattered whitecaps
bft.sea.4: small waves becoming longer, numerous whitecaps
bft.sea.5: moderate waves of longer form, many whitecaps, some spray
bft.sea.6: larger waves forming, whitecaps everywhere, more spray
bft.sea.7: sea heaps up, foam from breaking waves blown in streaks
bft.sea.8: moderately high waves, crests break into spindrift, foam in well-marked streaks
bft.sea.9: high waves, crests begin to topple, spray may reduce visibility
bft.sea.10: very high waves with overhanging crests, sea white with foam, visibility reduced
bft.sea.11: exceptionally high waves, sea covered with foam patches, visibility poor
bft.sea.12: air filled with foam and spray, sea completely white, visibility very poor
calc.notices.title: Corrections log: Notices to Mariners and NAVAREA
calc.notices.caption: Record the Notices to Mariners weekly editions, notice numbers and NAVAREA warnings you have received — the app shows missing numbers and what has not been applied yet. Saved on this device.
calc.notices.start_hint: If you keep the log from the start of the year, enter 1. Leave empty to check gaps from the first number you entered.
calc.notices.need_number: Enter at least one number: edition, notice or NAVAREA.
calc.notices.empty: No entries for {year} yet. Add the first edition you received above.
calc.notices.disclaimer: A self-check helper: it only checks the numbering of what you have entered. The official record is the chart and publication correction log and the procedure set by your company SMS. Data is stored only on this device.
err.notices.bad_number: Could not read the number “{token}”. Separate numbers with commas and ranges with a hyphen: 125-131.
err.notices.bad_range: Invalid range “{token}”: the first number must be lower than the second.
tooltip.nl-issue: Number of the weekly Notices to Mariners edition — numbered from the start of the year. After adding, the next number is filled in.
tooltip.nl-notices: Notice numbers in this edition: comma-separated, consecutive ones as a range, e.g. 125-131, 133.
tooltip.nl-navarea: NAVAREA navigational warning numbers (EGC/NAVTEX or in-force list), e.g. 045, 046 or 045-048.
tooltip.nl-area: The NAVAREA you receive warnings for (e.g. I — North-East Atlantic). Label only.

calc.sun.title: Compass error by the Sun
calc.sun.caption: True bearing of the Sun by azimuth or amplitude — no almanac or tables, fully offline
calc.sun.amp_hint: Take the bearing when the Sun's centre is on the celestial horizon: the lower limb about 2/3 of a diameter above the visible horizon.
calc.sun.warn_below: The Sun is below the horizon — no bearing can be taken at this moment. Check the date, UTC time and longitude.
calc.sun.warn_high: Sun's altitude is above 30° — azimuth-ring bearings are less accurate; observe when the Sun is low.
calc.sun.warn_amplitude_limb: The amplitude applies to the Sun's centre on the celestial horizon — lower limb about 2/3 of a diameter above the visible horizon.
calc.sun.warn_high_lat: Above 60° latitude the bearing changes quickly at sunrise/sunset — the amplitude method is less accurate.
calc.sun.disclaimer: Sun's coordinates by Meeus' algorithm (about 0.01° accuracy). An aid only: log the compass error from several observations.
err.celestial.bad_datetime: Enter the UTC date and time.
err.celestial.no_rise_set: At this latitude on this date the Sun does not rise or set (polar day or night).
tooltip.sun-date: Greenwich (UTC) date, not ship's date. Near midnight UTC it may differ from ship's date.
tooltip.sun-time: UTC time of the bearing — from the chronometer or GPS. A 4-minute time error gives about 1° bearing error with a high Sun.
tooltip.sun-event: Sunrise — the Sun in the east; sunset — in the west.
tooltip.sun-lat-deg: DR or observed latitude at the time of observation (GPS, chart).
tooltip.sun-lon-deg: Ship's longitude at the time of observation. Needed for the Sun's local hour angle: 1° of longitude error ≈ 1° of LHA.
tooltip.sun-cb: Bearing of the Sun's centre taken with an azimuth circle (or shadow pin) on the gyro repeater or magnetic compass.
tooltip.sun-var: Magnetic variation from the chart, corrected for the year. Fill in for a magnetic compass to get deviation. For a gyro leave empty — the error is the gyro error.
trainer.title: COLREGs trainer: who gives way?
trainer.intro: Encounters by day, by night from lights, and in fog. Choose an answer — the scene shows the correct manoeuvre and the explanation links to the rule.
trainer.who.him: He gives way, I keep my course and speed
trainer.opt.stand_on: Keep course and speed — it is his duty to give way
trainer.opt.sound5: Give at least five short and rapid blasts and, if he does not act, take action myself — but not alter to port
trainer.opt.port_towards: Alter to port to clear him faster
trainer.opt.keep_to_end: Keep course and speed to the end — I am the stand-on vessel
trainer.ask.fog_bow: Your manoeuvre, if you decide to alter course?
trainer.ask.fog_quarter: Your manoeuvre, if you decide to alter course?
trainer.ask.sound_starboard: Which signal do you give when altering?
trainer.grade_a: Excellent — you know the steering and sailing rules well.
trainer.grade_b: Good. Retry the mistakes and open the rules from the links.
trainer.grade_c: Worth revising COLREGs Part B (Rules 4–19) and Rules 21–28 on lights and shapes.
trainer.disclaimer: Training situations are simplified: in a real encounter decisions depend on the whole situation (Rules 2, 7, 8). The trainer does not replace knowing the full text of COLREGs 1972.
trainer.q.head_on: Daytime, good visibility. You are a power-driven vessel. Dead ahead a vessel is coming straight at you: you see her masts in line.
trainer.e.head_on: Head-on situation (Rule 14): each vessel alters course to starboard so that each passes on the port side of the other. There is no stand-on vessel here — both act.
trainer.q.cross_stbd: A power-driven vessel is crossing from your starboard side to port; her bearing is steady.
trainer.e.cross_stbd: Crossing situation (Rule 15): the vessel which has the other on her own starboard side keeps out of the way — that is you. The give-way vessel takes early and substantial action (Rule 16) and avoids crossing ahead: alter to starboard and pass astern of her.
trainer.q.cross_port: A power-driven vessel is crossing from your port side to starboard; her bearing is steady.
trainer.e.cross_port: You see her on your port side, so she has you on her starboard side and gives way (Rule 15). You are the stand-on vessel and keep course and speed (Rule 17(a)(i)), while watching and ready to act if she does not.
trainer.q.overtaking: You are catching up a slow vessel on the same course, approaching from more than 22.5° abaft her beam.
trainer.e.overtaking: An overtaking vessel keeps out of the way of the vessel being overtaken (Rule 13(a)), notwithstanding the other rules of Part B. You may pass on either side without creating a close-quarters situation.
trainer.q.overtaken: A vessel on your starboard quarter, from abaft the beam, is quickly catching you up on the same course.
trainer.e.overtaken: The vessel catching up is the overtaking vessel (Rule 13(b)): she keeps clear until finally past and clear. You keep your course and speed (Rule 17).
trainer.q.night_head_on: Night. Dead ahead you see two masthead lights nearly in line and both sidelights — green and red.
trainer.e.night_head_on: Masthead lights in or nearly in line and/or both sidelights indicate a head-on situation (Rule 14(b)). Both vessels alter to starboard and pass port to port.
trainer.q.night_green: Night. On your port bow you see two masthead lights and a green sidelight; the bearing is steady.
trainer.e.night_green: Green is her starboard side: she is crossing from port to starboard and has you on her starboard side, so she gives way (Rule 15). You keep course and speed, watching closely (Rule 17).
trainer.q.night_red: Night. On your starboard bow you see two masthead lights and a red sidelight; the bearing is steady.
trainer.e.night_red: Red is her port side: she is crossing from starboard to port and is on your starboard side. You give way (Rule 15): alter to starboard and pass astern of her.
trainer.q.night_stern: Night. Dead ahead there is a single white light and you are closing it fast.
trainer.e.night_stern: A single white light ahead while closing is the sternlight of a vessel on the same course (135° arc, Rule 21(c)). You are overtaking and keep out of the way (Rule 13). At night a vessel is overtaking if she can see only the sternlight of the other (Rule 13(b)).
trainer.q.sail_port: You are a power-driven vessel. On your port bow a yacht under sail only is crossing your course.
trainer.e.sail_port: A power-driven vessel keeps out of the way of a sailing vessel (Rule 18(a)(iv)), whichever side she is on. Rule 15 (crossing) applies only between two power-driven vessels. Here the easiest action is to slow down and let the yacht pass.
trainer.q.fishing: You are a power-driven vessel. On your port bow a trawler is moving slowly; by day she shows two cones with apexes together.
trainer.e.fishing: Two cones with apexes together mean a vessel engaged in fishing (Rule 26). A power-driven vessel keeps out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing (Rule 18(a)(iii)) — give her a wide berth, remembering the trawl astern.
trainer.q.nuc_night: Night. Almost dead ahead there are two all-round red lights in a vertical line and no sidelights.
trainer.e.nuc_night: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line — a vessel not under command (Rule 27(a)); no sidelights means she is not making way. A power-driven vessel keeps out of her way (Rule 18(a)(i)).
trainer.q.ram: You are a power-driven vessel. On your port bow a slow vessel shows ball — diamond — ball by day.
trainer.e.ram: Ball, diamond, ball in a vertical line — a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (Rule 27(b)). A power-driven vessel keeps out of her way (Rule 18(a)(ii)).
trainer.q.cbd: You are a power-driven vessel. A large tanker is approaching slightly to port; by day she shows a cylinder.
trainer.e.cbd: A cylinder — a vessel constrained by her draught (Rule 28). Any vessel other than one not under command or restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shall, if the circumstances admit, avoid impeding her safe passage (Rule 18(d)(i)).
trainer.q.sail_tacks: You are on a sailing yacht with the wind on your port side. On your starboard bow another yacht has the wind on her starboard side; courses are crossing.
trainer.e.sail_tacks: When sailing vessels have the wind on different sides, the one with the wind on the port side keeps out of the way (Rule 12(a)(i)) — that is you. Bear away and pass astern of her.
trainer.q.sail_windward: You are on a sailing yacht; both yachts have the wind on the port side. The other yacht is to starboard of you, to leeward; courses converge.
trainer.e.sail_windward: When both have the wind on the same side, the vessel to windward keeps out of the way of the vessel to leeward (Rule 12(a)(ii)). You are to windward, so you give way — for example ease sheets, slow down and let her pass.
trainer.q.sail_overtaking: You are on a sailing yacht catching up a slow power-driven vessel on the same course.
trainer.e.sail_overtaking: Rule 13 applies “notwithstanding anything contained in the Rules of Part B, Sections I and II”, i.e. even against Rule 18: an overtaking sailing vessel keeps out of the way of the power-driven vessel being overtaken.
trainer.q.overtaken_by_sail: You are a power-driven vessel at slow speed. A sailing yacht is catching you up from your port quarter.
trainer.e.overtaken_by_sail: The yacht is the overtaking vessel and keeps out of your way (Rule 13). That she is under sail does not matter: Rule 18 does not apply to overtaking. You keep your course and speed.
trainer.q.narrow_channel: You are a large vessel that can safely navigate only within a narrow channel. On your port side a sailing yacht is about to cross the channel ahead of you.
trainer.e.narrow_channel: A sailing vessel (like a vessel of less than 20 m) shall not impede the passage of a vessel which can safely navigate only within a narrow channel or fairway (Rule 9(b)), and shall not cross it if that impedes such a vessel (Rule 9(d)). You still keep a lookout and, in doubt, give five short blasts.
trainer.q.fog_bow: Restricted visibility, fog. Radar shows an echo forward of the starboard beam, range decreasing; you have determined that a close-quarters situation is developing. You are not overtaking her.
trainer.e.fog_bow: In fog there is no stand-on vessel: Rule 19 requires both to act. For a vessel forward of the beam (other than one being overtaken), avoid an alteration of course to port (Rule 19(d)(i)). Altering to starboard is correct; reducing speed is also an option.
trainer.q.fog_quarter: Fog. An echo on your starboard quarter, abaft the beam, is approaching fast; radar shows a close-quarters situation developing.
trainer.e.fog_quarter: Rule 19(d)(ii): avoid an alteration of course towards a vessel abeam or abaft the beam. The target is on the starboard quarter, so do not turn to starboard (towards her); altering to port takes you away.
trainer.q.stand_on_act: A vessel on your port bow is crossing; she must give way but keeps her course and speed, and the range is closing fast.
trainer.e.stand_on_act: If in doubt whether the give-way vessel is taking action, give at least five short and rapid blasts (Rule 34(d)). The stand-on vessel may act herself as soon as it is apparent the other is not taking action (Rule 17(a)(ii)) and must act when collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel alone (17(b)). If circumstances admit, she shall not alter to port for a vessel on her own port side (17(c)).
trainer.q.sound_starboard: Good visibility, vessels in sight of one another. You give way to a vessel on your starboard side and alter to starboard.
trainer.e.sound_starboard: Rule 34(a): a power-driven vessel under way manoeuvring in sight of another vessel gives one short blast — “I am altering my course to starboard”, two — “to port”, three — “I am operating astern propulsion”. Five short blasts is the doubt signal (34(d)); one prolonged blast is for nearing a bend (34(e)).
calc.sun.no_compass_bearing: Enter the compass bearing to get the compass error
err.common.empty_field: Fill in all fields with numbers — one of them is empty or invalid.
err.sailing.bad_latitude: Latitude must be between 0° and 90° (N or S).
err.sailing.pole_rhumb: A rhumb line is undefined at the pole — use great-circle sailing.
err.sailing.pole_crossing: With this course and distance the track passes the pole — rhumb-line DR is impossible.
err.noon_report.elapsed_hours_must_be_po: The reporting period must be longer than zero.
err.noon_report.negative_fuel: Distances and fuel quantities cannot be negative.
err.noon_report.zero_speed_no_eta: Distance run is 0 — time to go cannot be found from the average speed.
err.noon_report.consumed_exceeds_rob: Consumption exceeds the fuel on board — check ROB and consumption.
err.tides.target_outside_half_cycle: The time is outside the half-cycle (between low and high water) — the rule of twelfths does not apply.
err.ukc.bad_channel_area: Channel and midship section areas must be greater than zero.
err.ukc.blockage_too_high: The midship section area exceeds the channel area — check the data.
err.ukc.bad_ship_data: Check the data: Cb must be between 0 and 1, speed cannot be negative.
err.anchor.bad_input: Depth and hawse height cannot be negative; ratio and shackle length must be greater than zero.
err.roll_period.period_must_be_positive: The rolling period must be greater than zero.
err.roll_period.beam_must_be_positive: The beam must be greater than zero.
err.roll_period.ship_data_must_be_positi: Waterline length and draft must be greater than zero (or leave both empty).
err.blind_distance.eye_not_above_obstruc: The observer's eye must be higher than the top of the obstruction.
err.bunker.table_too_short: The calibration table needs at least two rows.
err.bunker.sounding_out_of_range: The sounding is outside the calibration table — extend the table.
err.bunker.density_must_be_positive: Density must be greater than zero.
err.sextant.negative_height: Height of eye cannot be negative.
err.notices.range_too_large: The gap between numbers is too large (over 5000) — check for a typo.
err.drill.bad_date: One of the drills has no valid date of last performance.
calc.stability.list_over_10: List over 10° — the small-angle formula is no longer accurate; use the ship's GZ curve.
calc.roll_gm.length_label: Waterline length Lwl, m — for the IMO formula
calc.roll_gm.draft_label: Mean draft d, m — for the IMO formula
tooltip.rg-length: Optional. With Lwl and draft the IMO formula is used (IS Code 2008): T = 2·C·B/√GM. Without them a simplified f = 0.797 is used, which overstates GM for ships longer than ~70 m.
tooltip.rg-draft: Mean draft at the time of the roll test, metres. Needed together with Lwl for the IMO formula.
err.converters.coords.out_of_range: Latitude cannot exceed 90°, longitude cannot exceed 180°.
err.converters.coords.minutes_out_of_ran: Minutes and seconds must be less than 60.
err.true_wind.negative_speed: Wind and ship speeds cannot be negative.

trainer.ask.sound_port: Which signal do you give when altering course?
trainer.ask.fog_signal: Which sound signal do you give?
trainer.q.anchored_day: Daytime. Right ahead lies a vessel with a black ball hoisted forward. The range is closing.
trainer.e.anchored_day: A black ball forward means a vessel at anchor (Rule 30(a)). She is not underway and cannot give way, so it is you who must keep clear — early and at a safe distance (Rule 8). The steering and sailing Rules 13–18 do not apply to a vessel at anchor.
trainer.q.anchored_night: Night. Right ahead you see two white lights: one higher at one end, the other lower and some distance from it. No sidelights; the bearing is steady and the range is closing.
trainer.e.anchored_night: A vessel of 50 m or more at anchor shows two all-round white lights: forward — higher, aft — lower (Rule 30(a)); no sidelights. A towing vessel shows masthead lights in a vertical line, not spread along the length, plus sidelights (Rule 24). Keep clear of the anchored vessel in good time.
trainer.q.aground_day: Daytime. Fine on the starboard bow lies a stopped vessel showing three black balls in a vertical line.
trainer.e.aground_day: Three balls in a vertical line — a vessel aground (Rule 30(d)(ii)); at night anchor lights plus two all-round red lights in a vertical line. A vessel at anchor shows one ball, a vessel not under command two balls (Rule 27(a)). Keep clear: there may be shallow water nearby.
trainer.q.nuc_day: You are a power-driven vessel. Almost right ahead is a vessel with no way on, showing two black balls in a vertical line.
trainer.e.nuc_day: Two balls in a vertical line — a vessel not under command (Rule 27(a)). A power-driven vessel keeps out of her way (Rule 18(a)(i)). Pass early and at a safe distance.
trainer.q.towing_day: A power-driven vessel on your starboard side crosses from right to left. She shows a diamond, and a barge follows on a long tow line. The bearing is steady.
trainer.e.towing_day: A diamond means the length of tow exceeds 200 m (Rule 24(a)(v)). A towing vessel has no special priority as such (unless restricted in her ability to manoeuvre), so Rule 15 applies: she is on your starboard side — you give way. Alter to starboard and pass astern of the tow — never between the tug and the tow.
trainer.q.towing_night: Night. On the starboard bow you see three white lights exactly in a vertical line and a red sidelight. The bearing is steady.
trainer.e.towing_night: Three masthead lights in a vertical line — a vessel towing with a length of tow over 200 m (Rule 24(a)(i)). Red is her port side: she is on your starboard side, crossing right to left. She has no special priority, so Rule 15 applies: you give way. Pass astern of the tow, not between the tug and the tow.
trainer.q.pilot_night: Night. On the port bow an all-round white light over a red one, with a green sidelight below. The bearing is steady.
trainer.e.pilot_night: White over red — a pilot vessel on pilotage duty (Rule 29(a)); when underway she also shows sidelights. Green is her starboard side: she sees you on her starboard side. A pilot vessel has no special priority, so Rule 15 applies: she gives way, you stand on.
trainer.q.trawler_night: Night. On the port bow an all-round green light over a white one and a green sidelight. The vessel is slowly crossing your course; the bearing is steady.
trainer.e.trawler_night: Green over white — a vessel engaged in trawling (Rule 26(b)). Although she is on your port side, Rule 15 does not apply: a power-driven vessel keeps out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing (Rule 18(a)(iii)). Alter to starboard and keep clear in good time.
trainer.q.fishing_other_night: Night. On the port bow a vessel is moving slowly: an all-round red light over an all-round white light.
trainer.e.fishing_other_night: Red over white — a vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling (Rule 26(c)), e.g. long-lining or netting. A pilot vessel is the other way round — white over red (Rule 29); a vessel not under command shows two reds (Rule 27). A power-driven vessel keeps out of her way (Rule 18).
trainer.q.cbd_night: Night. A large vessel approaches, slightly to port: three all-round red lights in a vertical line, a masthead light and both sidelights.
trainer.e.cbd_night: Three red lights in a vertical line — a vessel constrained by her draught (Rule 28). Any vessel other than one not under command or restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shall, if the circumstances admit, avoid impeding her safe passage (Rule 18(d)(i)). Act early so that she does not have to manoeuvre.
trainer.q.ram_night: Night. On the port bow a vessel moves slowly: red, white and red all-round lights in a vertical line, a masthead light and a green sidelight.
trainer.e.ram_night: Red — white — red in a vertical line — a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (Rule 27(b)); when making way she also shows masthead and sidelights. Although she is on your port side, a power-driven vessel keeps out of her way (Rule 18(a)(ii)).
trainer.q.sail_night: Night. You are a power-driven vessel. On the port bow you see only a green sidelight, with no masthead light above it. The bearing is steady.
trainer.e.sail_night: A sidelight without a masthead light — a sailing vessel (Rule 25(a)): only power-driven vessels show masthead lights. So Rule 15 does not apply: a power-driven vessel keeps out of the way of a sailing vessel (Rule 18(a)(iv)), whichever side she is on.
trainer.q.motorsailer: Daytime. On your port bow a yacht with sails set crosses your course, showing a cone point downwards. The bearing is steady.
trainer.e.motorsailer: A cone point downwards — a vessel proceeding under sail and also propelled by machinery (Rule 25(e)). Such a vessel counts as power-driven, and Rule 18 does not apply to her. Rule 15 applies: she sees you on her starboard side and gives way. You stand on.
trainer.q.fishing_vs_sail: You are on a sailing yacht. On the starboard bow a trawler moves slowly, showing two cones with their points together. The courses cross.
trainer.e.fishing_vs_sail: A sailing vessel underway keeps out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing (Rule 18(b)(iii)); two cones points together mean a vessel engaged in fishing (Rule 26). The priority a sailing vessel has over a power-driven vessel does not help here.
trainer.q.sound_port: Good visibility. Right ahead lies a vessel at anchor. You decide to pass leaving her to starboard and alter course to port.
trainer.e.sound_port: Rule 34(a): a power-driven vessel underway, manoeuvring in sight of other vessels, signals: one short blast — 'I am altering my course to starboard', two short blasts — 'to port', three short blasts — 'I am operating astern propulsion'.
trainer.q.sound_astern: Good visibility. Close ahead is a vessel not under command. To take the way off, you put the engine astern.
trainer.e.sound_astern: Three short blasts — 'I am operating astern propulsion' (Rule 34(a)(iii)). One short — altering to starboard, two — to port; five or more short — doubt about the other vessel's intentions (Rule 34(d)).
trainer.q.fog_signal: Fog. You are a power-driven vessel making way through the water.
trainer.e.fog_signal: Rule 35(a): a power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes. Two prolonged — underway but stopped (35(b)). One prolonged followed by two short — not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre, constrained by draught, sailing, fishing and towing vessels (35(c)).
app.ios.install_title: Add AZIMUTH to your Home Screen
app.ios.install_lead: The app will open full screen like a regular one and work without internet.
app.ios.step1: Tap Share in Safari — the square with an arrow. On recent iOS versions it is under the “•••” button.
app.ios.step2: Choose “Add to Home Screen” and tap Add.
app.ios.step3: Open AZIMUTH from the new icon and wait for it to load. Internet is needed only this first time.
app.ios.step4: Enter your key there: the Home Screen app has its own device code.
app.ios.not_safari: No Share button? The page is open inside another app — open it in Safari.
app.ios.continue_btn: View the demo in the browser
app.ios.lic_note: On iPhone and iPad the key is entered in the app opened from the Home Screen icon. Install it first — it takes a minute.
app.ios.keep_icon: Do not remove the AZIMUTH icon from the Home Screen: activation and logs are removed with it and the device code changes.
app.ios.share_failed: Could not open the Share sheet. Please try again.
